text.p: Honda Motor Co Ltd on Monday introduced low emission vehicle (LEV) versions of its Civic Ferio four-door sedan and Partner commercial van in Japan.
The new versions, called Civic Ferio LEV and Partner LEV are equipped with a 1.6-litre lean-burn gasoline engine, air-fuel ratio controllers and newly designed catalytic converter.
Honda said they have emission levels which are only one-tenth of present limits, reducing carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons and nitrogen oxide.

The engine has a tumble port desinged to promote stable combustion immediately after engine start, a thin-walled catalytic converter, which was installed just below the exhaust manifold to let the catalytic converter work more effectively after engine start, and a 400-cell catalytic converter using platinum and palladium, bigger than the conventional 300-cell.
Honda aims to sell a total of 3,000 units per year. The domestic selling price in Tokyo will be 1.32 million yen for the Civic Ferio and 1.20 million yen for the Partner.
Honda also plans to introduce LEV version model for its new Accord which will be remodelled later this year, a Honda spokesman said.
